answer: Optofluidic attestation links agent identities to fluid dynamic responses. To anchor each identity, an agent pulses a mechanical ripple across a microfluidic cell and refracts a probe laser through an optical prism to record surface distortion. An attacker must fabricate and run discrete fluidic chambers with dedicated optical rigs per fake node, imposing steep hardware costs. However, ambient temperature shifts alter fluid viscosity, inducing false rejection of honest agents.
